pageData.heading: How to Make a Budget
pageData.para:
Budgeting doesn’t have to be complicated!
Here are some simple and practical steps to get you started.

whatIsBudgeting.heading: What is Budgeting ?
whatIsBudgeting.secPara:
Budgeting looks different for everyone, depending on individual needs and priorities.

Our research shows that taking the time to create and follow a budget can significantly improve your financial well-being.

Already confident in budgeting but need help with the numbers?
Check out our Budget Planner.
If you're just getting started and need some practical tips, keep reading!

understandingIncomeExpenses.heading: Understanding Your Income & Expenses
understandingIncomeExpenses.secPara:
Budgeting doesn’t mean giving up fun! It’s just about making sure your money isn’t disappearing faster than golgappas at a wedding.

The first step is to track every rupee, like a missing Tupperware lid—you know it’s somewhere, but where?

You need to figure out where your money comes from and where it goes.
More often, you’ll find it vanishing into Zomato orders and impulse shopping during sales.

Small, unnecessary expenses add up quickly like -
  • Gym membership you never use,
  • OTT subscriptions you got for just one show,
  • Chai/ Coffee stops that seem harmless but pile up.

The bottom line? Knowledge is power.
And in this case, it’s the power to stop your bank balance from looking like "a prepaid mobile recharge at the end of the month".

trackingIncome.text: Income isn’t just your salary—it includes any sources of money you regularly receive. This could be freelance earnings, interest from savings, or investments, side gigs, or even alimony.

categorizingExpenses.text:
Expenses are typically broken down into:

Fixed Expenses: Bills you pay monthly, like rent, utilities, loans, and subscriptions.
Variable Expenses: Costs that can fluctuate month-to-month, like groceries, entertainment, and shopping.
Discretionary Expenses: Non-essential spending, like dining out, hobbies, and vacations.

cards.heading: Plan SMART goals
cards.para:
• Specific,
  • Measurable,
  • Achievable,
  • Realistic, and
  • Time-bound goals help you stay on track.

    You may set a SMART goal like:
    "Save ₹5,000 per month for the next 6 months for my emergency fund."

cards.heading: Prioritize your Goals
cards.para:
It’s important to differentiate between short-term goals (1 year or less) and long-term goals (3-5 years or more).

Tips:
  • List your goals, then prioritize them based on urgency and importance.
  • Create a timeline for achieving each goal.

cards.heading: Essentials vs. Non-Essentials
cards.para: When you categorize your expenses, you take control of your spending. It helps you see where you’re spending too much, so you can adjust accordingly. Categorization makes budgeting more precise and efficient.

cards.heading: How to Categorize Your Expenses
cards.para:
• Essentials:Rent, bills, groceries, transportation.
  • Non-Essentials:Dining out, shopping, entertainment.
  • Savings & Investments:Emergency funds, retirement savings, mutual funds.

cards.heading: Benefits of Categorization
cards.para:
• Tracking:It becomes easier to see where your money goes.
  • Cut Back:: You can identify areas where you’re overspending and make adjustments.
  • Flexibility:Reassign funds to essential categories if needed, especially during uncertain times.

startBudgeting.heading: Start Budgeting Today
startBudgeting.secPara:
Creating a budget doesn’t have to be overwhelming. With these simple steps, you can begin to take control of your financial life, achieve your goals, and gain peace of mind.
